accepted.match: "justice" defined differently in justice and healthcare-ethics
accepted.reason: Compatible depth difference: the justice lesson defines the general philosophical family of concepts (distributive, retributive, procedural, corrective); healthcare-ethics defines the same term as the fourth biomedical principle applied to healthcare allocation. The healthcare lesson's definition is a domain application, not a contradiction.

accepted.match: "informed consent" defined differently in healthcare-ethics and technology-ethics
accepted.reason: Genuine domain-specific homonym: healthcare-ethics defines clinical informed consent (capacitated, informed, voluntary agreement to a medical intervention); technology-ethics defines consent to data processing, noting its limits in privacy literature. Both are correct in their owning lessons and do not contradict.

accepted.match: "responsibility gap" defined differently in technology-ethics and ai-ethics
accepted.reason: Compatible: both define the same concept — the difficulty of holding any human blameworthy for harms caused by automated/learning systems — with different wording (technology-ethics attributes the term to Matthias 2004; ai-ethics describes the situation in AI-specific terms). Same concept, complementary emphasis.
